activity: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
knowledge_domain: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
story:
Asher ran to the snack table at summer camp. He wanted the watermelon so much. But Miss Jo put up her hand. "Wash first, sweet pea," she said.

Asher looked at his hands. They had sand on them. He put one finger in his mouth. Yuck. Sand was gritty and bad. So he went to the little sink. He pushed the soap pump. Bubbles came out, big and white. Miss Jo sang a song while he rubbed. "Bubbles, bubbles, up and down. Bubbles, bubbles, all around." Asher sang too. The bubbles carried the sand away. He watched the sand go down, down, down the drain.

Then the team sat together on a cozy blanket. Asher held his watermelon slice. It was clean and sweet. "No sand today," said Asher. He smiled and took a big bite.

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Mya went to the library with her dad. The storytime room had soft blue mats. A lady named Miss Jo held up a card. "This is a library card," she said. "It lets you take books home."

Mya wanted a card so much. She waited in the line. One friend went first. Then another friend. Then it was Mya's turn. Miss Jo wrote Mya's name on a little card. Mya clapped her hands.

Mya picked a book about a striped cat. The cat had red stripes and yellow stripes. She held it tight. "This book is mine forever," she said.

Miss Jo shook her head. She showed Mya a paper pocket in the book. "The book goes home with you," she said. "Then you bring it back. Then Tom can read it too."

Tom was the boy with the blue shoes. Tom looked at the striped cat book. He wanted it too.

Mya looked at the book. She looked at Tom. She gave the book a big hug. Then she set it in her bag.

"Seven sleeps," said Miss Jo. "Then the book comes back."

At home, Mya counted the sleeps. One sleep. Two sleeps. Three sleeps. Four sleeps. Five sleeps. Six sleeps. Seven sleeps!

Mya carried the book back to Miss Jo. She set it in Miss Jo's hands. Then something surprising happened. Tom clapped for her. And on the table sat a new book. It was about paint. Bright paint, red and yellow, just like the cat.

"Ready for the next one?" asked Miss Jo.

"Yes," said Mya. "And Tom can have it after me."

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Luka sat in a big chair at the doctor's office. He wanted the fish sticker on the wall. But first, Doctor Amy said, "I need to check you." Luka looked at the sticker with his eyes. "Fish can swim," he said. "Can I have that fish?"

"One thing at a time," said Doctor Amy. She held up a small light. "Tell me what you see." Luka saw the light with his eyes. It blinked on and off. He covered one eye. The light looked the same. He uncovered it. Then the light looked different. Covering made it change! He tried both eyes. Now he saw two lights.

Next came the sounds. Doctor Amy rang a tiny bell. Luka heard it with his ears. Then he sniffed with his nose. "I smell soap," he said. He tasted an apple slice with his tongue. He touched the cool table with his fingers. "Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, fingers," he counted. "Five helpers." Doctor Amy smiled. "All five work great. Now look what I have." She held out the fish sticker. It was a fish by a tree, with brown roots under the ground. "For my best helper," she said. Luka stuck it on his shirt. "My fish can swim on me," he said.

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
story:
Jordan was at a restaurant with Mom and Dad. A big game was on the big screen. Everyone wore the team color, red. Jordan had a red hat and a red scarf. Even his boots were red.

Then the screen went dark. The game was frozen. The players did not move. "Oh no!" said Jordan. The whole room went quiet.

A waiter came by. He pressed a little button on his remote. The screen lit up. The players ran again. Jordan clapped and clapped.

Later, the screen froze one more time. Jordan waved his hand high. "Press the button!" he called. The waiter smiled and pressed it. The game came back, and everyone cheered. Dad lifted his cup. "Way to go, Jordan!"

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
story:
Iris wanted to wash her hands all by herself. She stood by the sink and looked up at the faucet. The faucet was shiny and silver. It had a red dot on one side and a blue dot on the other side.

"Can I turn it on?" she asked.

"Yes, but wait for me," said Dad. Dad came and stood close to her. He put his hand under the water first. "Let me check it," he said.

Iris waited. She saw Dad touch the water and nod. "Now it is warm, not hot," he said. "Cold, then warm. Hot water can hurt you."

Dad turned the shiny handle a tiny bit. First the water was cold. Iris touched it with one finger. Then Dad turned it more, just a little. The water got warm. Iris put both hands in. She rubbed the soap and made white bubbles.

She saw that the little red dot made hot water. She did not touch that side. Dad turned the red side for her, slowly and carefully.

"I can learn the dots," said Iris. She pointed to the blue dot. "Blue is for me."

"That's right," said Dad. He handed her the small towel. Iris dried her hands and hung the towel on the hook, all by herself.

"Good helper," said Dad. He lifted her down and held her hand as they walked out.

activity: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
knowledge_domain: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
story:
Liam stood in the school computer lab. He wanted to draw a big sun. But the tablet was dark and still. He touched the black screen. Nothing happened.

Miss Rosa knelt down next to him. She held his hand gently. "Push the round button," she said. "It lives at the bottom of the tablet." Liam found the round button. He pushed it with one finger. The screen lit up, all bright and yellow and blue. Liam laughed out loud.

Now he needed the drawing app. Miss Rosa showed him the little picture of a paintbrush. Liam tapped it once. Nothing. He tapped it again, slower this time. The white page opened. Liam dragged his finger across the glass. A thick green line followed his finger. He made a circle. He made rays, one by one. The tablet felt smooth and warm under his hand.

Then the bell rang. Time to go. Miss Rosa did not grab the tablet. She waited. Liam looked at his sun. He pressed the round button again. The screen went dark. He slid the tablet into its soft blue bag. He pulled the zipper. It was a tight fit, but he tugged it to the top.

Liam carried the bag with two hands. He set it in the basket by the door. "My sun is sleeping," he told Miss Rosa. She smiled and patted the bag. "See you tomorrow, sun."

activity: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
knowledge_domain: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
story:
Madison stood at the running track. She held a red beanbag. A hoop lay on the ground far away. She wanted the beanbag to land inside it. She threw it. The beanbag fell to the left. It missed the hoop. Madison frowned. She asked, "Where did it go?" Her dad said, "Try again." She looked at the hoop. She stood straight and faced it. She threw the beanbag straight ahead. It landed inside the hoop. "It went in!" she said.

Next, Dad rolled a big ball to her. She used one hand. The ball bounced off and rolled away. She asked, "Why did it fall?" She looked at her hands. She held out both hands. Dad rolled the ball again. She caught it with both hands. "I got it!" she said. Dad clapped. On her shirt was a little pig, and it bounced up and down as she jumped. "Can we go now?" she asked. Dad said, "Yes. Let's go home and swim."

activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
story:
Arlo woke up and looked out the window. The backyard was white. "Snow!" he shouted. "No school today," said Mom. "It is a snow day."

Arlo wanted to build a snowman. He put on his boots. Mom helped him tie his boots. She pulled the laces tight. Then they went outside. The snow was cold and soft. It squeaked under his feet.

Arlo patted a big snowball with his mittens. He patted it and patted it. "Why is it getting smaller?" he asked. Mom said, "Your hands are warm. Warm hands make snow melt." Arlo held his mittens on the snow. Drip, drip, drip. Little wet spots appeared. He gasped. His mittens made water!

Arlo took off one mitten and made a face in the snow. He pressed his warm thumb here and there. The snow melted into two eyes and a smile. Mom knelt down and gave the snowman a gentle pet on his cold head. "Good snowman," she said. Arlo laughed. Then he put his wet mitten back on and patted more snow.

activity: getting a first haircut at a salon
knowledge_domain: getting a first haircut at a salon
story:
Leon sat in a big chair at the hair salon. The chair was too big for him. His dad stood right beside him and held his hand.

"I don't want a haircut," said Leon. "I want my hair to stay on my head."

The hairdresser, Mia, smiled. "Watch what my scissors do," she said. "Snip, snip. One piece falls. Snip, snip. Two pieces fall."

Mia snipped near Leon's ear. A little piece of hair dropped down. It fell on the cape like a soft brown string. Leon watched it fall.

"Another one!" he said. "Snip, snip, three!"

Mia snipped again. More hair fell. It made a little pile on the floor. Leon saw that each snip made one piece fall. He turned his head to see better.

"Look, Dad! Snip, snip, four pieces!"

Dad laughed. "You are watching so well."

Soon the snipping stopped. Mia brushed Leon's neck with a soft brush. Leon looked in the mirror. His hair was short now. He touched it with his hand. It felt fuzzy like a peach.

"I have a new head," said Leon.

"You have the same head," said Dad. "Just less hair on it. You look so big."

At home, Mom was going to cook dinner. Leon ran to her. "Mom! My hair fell down, snip by snip!"

Mom hugged him close. "My big boy," she said.

Leon yawned. All that watching had made him tired. He leaned his fuzzy head on Mom's shoulder.

"Snip, snip," he said softly, and closed his eyes.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Owen did not want to go to the doctor. He was grumpy all morning. "No doctor," he said. "No shot, no cold thing."

Mom drove anyway. "We will get bread after," she said. "Warm bread."

At the office, Owen sat very still. He wanted to hide.

The doctor came in. "Hello, Owen!" she said. "Let's play a game. We use our body parts to find things out."

First she held up a card. "Close one eye. What do you see?" Owen looked with his eyes. "A duck!" he said. "A silly duck with a hat!"

Next she turned a knob. Beep, beep. Owen heard it with his ears. "I hear it!" he said. "It goes fast!"

Then she held a little jar. "Sniff this." Owen smelled it with his nose. "Yuck! That smells like socks!"

The doctor laughed. "Open wide." Owen stuck out his tongue. She looked, but he did not taste anything. "Say ahhh." "Ahhh!"

Last came the cold circle. Owen touched it with his tummy. "Brrr!" he said. "That is cold as snow!"

Then the doctor gave him blocks. "You can build a tower while we talk." Owen built it tall. Too tall. It fell down. Boom!

"Uh oh," said Owen.

"That is okay," said the doctor. "Now watch this." She spun the top block. It wobbled. Then the whole tower wobbled. Then it tipped.

Owen gasped. He built it again. This time he made a wide bottom. He spun the top block. The tower wobbled. But it did not fall.

"Look, Mom! Wide bottom, no fall!"

Then the doctor said, "All done, Owen." No shot today.

Owen got a dinosaur sticker. "I like the doctor," he said. "Can we come back tomorrow?"

Mom laughed. "Let's go get that bread. You can smell it all the way home."

activity: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
knowledge_domain: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
story:
Anna sat at the table. The soup was hot. She wanted to eat it now.

Papa held up his hand. "We say our words first," he said. "Then we eat."

Anna pouted. The steam went up, up, up. "I want soup," she said.

Mama pointed at the steam. "Watch the steam," she said. "It rises like our words."

Anna watched the steam. It went up in little curls. Papa put his hand out. Anna put her small hand in it. Mama held Papa's hand too.

Then they said their words. "Thank you for our food. Thank you for our family." Anna said the parts she knew. "Thank you for soup. Thank you for cow milk."

Papa laughed. "Yes, thank you for cow milk," he said.

Then something surprising happened. A voice said, "Thank you from Grandma too!" Grandma was on the phone!

Anna clapped her hands. "Grandma said it too!"

Now every night, Anna held hands first. Then she said the words. Then everyone ate together.

"Bless our soup," Anna said. "Bless Grandma far away."

"Grandma can hear us," said Mama. "Listen."

The phone made a happy sound. "I hear you, young lady," said Grandma. "Amen!"

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Edouard sits on the soft red rug at school. He holds a book about a pet dog. The pages feel smooth. The book smells like paper and glue. Edouard opens the cover. He sees small black marks on the page. "What are those marks?" he asks. "Those marks are words," says his teacher, Miss Lily. "Words tell the story."

Edouard turns the pages. He starts at the front. He goes to the back. One page, two pages, three pages. The dog finds a tight little hole. The dog digs. The dog is happy. Edouard hugs the book. He wants to keep it forever.

"Can I take this book home?" he asks. "Yes, you can borrow it," says Miss Lily. "But we must bring it back on Friday." On Friday, Edouard puts the book in the basket. His friend Sam picks it up next. "New reader!" says Edouard, and he claps his hands.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story:
Claire loved the bean game at daycare. Yesterday she planted a bean in a little cup. She gave it water and set it on the sunny windowsill.

Today Claire ran to the window. "Look, look," she said. The bean was still brown and round. Nothing had grown. Miss Pat smiled. "Not yet. Roots grow first, under the dirt. That takes time. Let's wait."

So they waited. Claire played blocks with Ben. Later she looked at the cup again. Still brown. Still round. The sky outside was cloudy. "Tomorrow," said Miss Pat. "Come back tomorrow."

Tomorrow came. Claire ran to the window. A small green sprout stood up out of the dirt! "It grew!" said Claire. She tapped the cup gently. Miss Pat brought more water. "Now we wait again," she said.

Claire grinned. "More tomorrow," she said, and set the cup back in the sun.

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
story:
Zoey wanted to build a house for her toy fish at daycare. But the blocks kept rolling away. Why did they roll? Zoey looked closely. Those blocks were round like balls. Round things roll!

She needed blocks that would stay still. She found a block with flat sides. It had four sides, all the same. She stacked it. It did not roll. "Square, square, stay right there," she said.

Next she found a long, flat block. It had four sides too, but two were long and two were short. She stacked it on the square block. It sat nice and still. Then she found a block with only three sides. It looked like a little roof. On it went, up on top. Pointy side up!

Zoey patted the tower. "My fish has a house," she said. Miss Ana smiled and pulled a cushion over. "Here is a round pond for your fish." The round cushion did not roll. It was soft and flat. Zoey placed the fish on top. "Round like you," she whispered. "But you stay still too."

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
story:
Elizabeth wants to paint a butterfly at daycare. She sees the paint jars on the high shelf. They are too far up. She jumps. She jumps again. No paint.

She walks to Teacher Nan. "Please help me get the paint," she says. Teacher Nan smiles. She brings the jar down. "Thank you," says Elizabeth.

She paints one wing. She paints two wings. Then paint drips. It lands on Ben's paper. His paper has a big red spot now. "Sorry, Ben," says Elizabeth. Ben makes a face. Then he laughs. "It looks like a red sun," he says. He adds yellow all around it.

Elizabeth makes the wings straight and purple. One, two, three, four spots on each wing. "It is a magic butterfly," she says. "Let's pretend it can fly." She holds it up. It waves in the air. "It says please and thank you too," says Ben. Elizabeth giggles. The butterfly flaps around the table and lands on her nose.

activity: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
knowledge_domain: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
story:
Alexander stood at the bus stop with Grandma. The big yellow bus would come soon. But Alexander's coat was not on yet. It sat on the bench like a sleepy turtle. "Can I do it myself?" he asked. Grandma smiled. "Try," she said.

Alexander pushed one arm in. Then the other arm. The coat hung crooked. Why? He looked down. One side was inside out! He pulled it off and shook it. Now the coat looked right. He pushed his arms in again. This time it fit. He found the zipper pull and pushed it up, up, up. Zzzzzip! It closed all the way to his chin.

"Look, Grandma!" said Alexander. "I did it!" Just then the bus came around the corner. Alexander was not too cold, and not too tired of waiting. He climbed the steps holding Grandma's hand. The turtle coat on the bench was gone. Alexander was wearing it. He had won the zipper all by himself.

activity: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
knowledge_domain: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
story:
Grandpa came to stay for a whole week. Olivier wanted to show him the park. "We will go every day," said Olivier.

On Monday they went to the big slide. On Tuesday they fed the ducks. But on Wednesday, rain fell. Olivier looked out the window. "The park is all wet," he said. "What can we do now?"

Grandpa smiled. "We can cook," he said. Grandpa cracked the eggs. Olivier stirred the bowl from his tall chair. Then Grandpa held the pan, and Olivier watched the pancakes puff up. "The pan made them big," said Olivier. "How does it do that?"

On Thursday the sun came back. Off they went to the park. Olivier found a big puddle. He dropped in one little stone. Plip! The water made rings. Then he dropped a big stone. Sploosh! The rings got big too. "Grandpa, come see!" he called. "Big stone, big rings!"

On Friday they made a sign for Grandpa's door. It said "Olivier's Grandpa" with a drawing of the park. Grandpa hung it up with a nail and his hammer, and Olivier held the sign steady.

On Sunday night Grandpa packed his bag. "Next time," said Olivier, "we drop the big stone first." Grandpa laughed and zipped the bag closed.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Eleanor ran to the swing. But the swing was wet. Rain had made a big puddle under it.

Eleanor looked with her eyes. The water shone in the sun. She touched it with her hand. It was cold and shiny. She sniffed with her nose. The wet slide smelled like rain. A bird sang, and she heard it with her ears.

Then a curly dog ran by. It shook its fur. Water flew everywhere. The water landed on the swing. The swing dried in the sun.

Eleanor waited. She touched the swing again. It was dry now. "Mama, look," she said. "The sun dried it." A small child sat alone by the sandbox, looking sad. Eleanor gave the child her hat. Then she climbed on the swing. "Whee," she said.

activity: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
knowledge_domain: to say a family blessing or greeting before a shared meal
story:
Henri stood by the big table at the hall. Everyone held hands in a circle. Papa held Henri's little hand. Henri wanted to say the words too, but he did not know them yet. The words felt too long and too thick, like a big sandwich he could not bite.

Papa said the blessing, one line at a time. "Thank you for our food." Henri listened close. "Thank you for our family." Henri opened his mouth. "Thank... you," he said. Mama smiled at him. Grandpa squeezed his hand.

Then it was time to eat. But Grandpa did not pick up his spoon. He looked at Henri and waited. Henri took a big breath. "Thank you for our food," he said. "Thank you for our family." Then Grandpa picked up his spoon. Then Mama did. Then everyone ate together.

Henri looked down the long table. When he said the words, the food started. It was like pushing a swing and the swing went. Papa put warm bread on Henri's plate. Henri took a bite. "Again next time," said Papa. "Yes," said Henri. "Me first."

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
story:
Sofia carried her swim bag down to the beach pool. Her towel had furry stripes on it. It was soft and warm.

A boy named Max was already in the pool. He kicked his legs fast. Then he zoomed forward like a little boat. Sofia watched him with wide eyes.

"I want to zoom too," she said. "How did you do that?" Max laughed. "Kick hard and see!"

Sofia held the pool wall with both hands. Then she kicked her legs. Splash, splash, splash! Her feet made white bubbles. And she felt herself slide forward through the water!

She kicked some more. She slid even farther. The water pushed her along, all the way to Max. He clapped his hands. "You zoomed!"

Sofia turned around and kicked back the other way. She zoomed to the wall. She zoomed to Max. She zoomed again and again.

"Look, Dad!" she called. Dad waved from his beach chair. Sofia kicked her fastest kick of all. The bubbles flew up around her like snow.

"Race you to the steps!" said Max. Sofia grinned and kicked.

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
story:
Bennett ran into the pool changing room. His swimsuit was all wet. Drip, drip, drip went the water on the floor. It made a little puddle by his feet.

Bennett looked down at the puddle. Where did the water come from? He stood very still. The drips came from his wet suit. When he moved, the drips moved too.

Bennett was sad. His clothes were in his bag. If the wet suit went in the bag, the bag would get all wet inside. He thought and thought.

Then he had an idea. He squeezed his swimsuit with both hands. Water ran out of it and down the drain. He squeezed until it stopped dripping. "All done," he said. Now the suit could keep the bag nice and dry.

Bennett put the suit in the bag. He picked it up. Not one drip fell. He smiled and ran out to find Daddy. "Look, my bag is dry," he said.

activity: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
knowledge_domain: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
story:
Grandma was coming to stay! Anna ran to the kitchen. "One week," said Mama. "Seven whole days."

Anna wanted to make Grandma a surprise. She took out paper and glue. She made a card. It was messy. Glue was on her hands. Glue was on the table. Glue was on one cup!

Then Anna saw something. The glue dripped down. It dripped onto the floor. Papa slipped a little. "Whoa," said Papa. "The floor is sticky!"

Anna looked at the sticky spot. Her messy glue did that. Papa wiped it with a wet cloth. The stickiness went away.

"I can fix it too," said Anna. She wiped the cup. She wiped the table. Clean, clean, clean.

The doorbell rang. Grandma was here! Anna held up her card. "For you," said Anna. "One card, seven days."

Grandma gave her a big hug.

activity: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
knowledge_domain: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
story:
Brielle woke up and wanted to play outside. But first she had to pick her clothes. She did not know what to wear.

She looked out the window. The sun was shining. It was sunny. So she put on a little hat. The sun was bright on her nose.

Then the sky turned gray. Rain began to fall. It was rainy now. Brielle took off her hat. She put on her rain boots instead. She met her boots by the door. They were yellow and shiny.

The rain stopped. The wind began to blow. It was windy! The wind blew the leaves fast across the yard. Brielle's hat flew off the hook. She laughed and put on her warm coat.

Then something soft and white fell from the sky. It was snow! Brielle put on her mittens. She put on her big puffy coat.

Mom opened the door. "Brr, look at you," said Mom. Brielle ran outside. She made one small snowball and held it up high. "It's snowy!" she said. Mom took a picture of her in the soft white yard.Brielle woke up. She looked out the window. The sun was shining. It was sunny today.

She wanted to wear her yellow hat. But where was it? She could not find it. Brielle met her cat, Mila, near the couch. Mila was sleeping on something soft. It was the yellow hat!

Brielle put on the hat. She went outside. The sun felt warm on her nose. She did not need a coat.

Then the wind came. It was windy. The wind blew her hat away. The hat flew fast across the grass. Brielle chased it. She caught it and held it tight.

Then rain began to fall. It was rainy now. Brielle ran inside. Mom gave her red boots and a raincoat. Brielle stomped in small puddles. Splash, splash.

Next, soft white snow fell down. It was snowy. Mom put warm mittens on Brielle's hands. Brielle patted the snow. "More hat," she said, and put the hat back on her head. The wind could not take it now.

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
story:
Eliana was three today. The community hall had balloons and paper snowflakes on the walls. They looked like soft white snow. There was a cake with thick pink frosting. Everyone sang the birthday song. Daddy lit three little candles with a match. He stepped back and stood by Eliana.

Then one candle went out. Eliana looked. A big fan was blowing on the cake. The fan made air move. The moving air blew out the candle. "Why did it go out?" Eliana asked. Grandma pointed at the fan. "The wind from the fan did it," she said. Daddy turned the fan off. He lit the candle again. This time it stayed lit. All three candles glowed.

Eliana took a big breath. She blew out all three candles herself. Everyone clapped. Then Eliana slid her fingers through the thick frosting and licked them. "Best cake ever," she said.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Riley went to the park with her dad. She wanted to find something special for show-and-tell. What could she find?

First she used her eyes. Her eyes saw a red leaf by the bench. She picked it up. Then her ears heard a sound. "Tweet, tweet!" A little bird sat in the tree. "Hello, bird," said Riley.

Next her nose smelled something sweet. Mmm! Dad was holding a picnic bag. Inside were strawberries. Riley used her tongue to taste one. Sweet and juicy! Her hands touched the grass. It was soft and a little dirty. Her hair got dirty too when she rolled down the hill. "You need a bath tonight," said Dad, and he laughed.

Riley put the red leaf in her pocket. Then the wind began to blow. The leaf went up, up, up! It flew right onto the bird's branch. The bird hopped onto the leaf. "Look, Dad!" said Riley. "The bird likes my leaf too."

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Elliot wanted to play house. He had a soft gray duck under his arm. "You be my baby," he told the duck.

He set the duck in a box. The box tipped over. The duck fell out! "Oh no," said Elliot. He tried again. The box tipped again. The duck fell on the rug.

Elliot looked around the room. He saw his big blanket. He pulled it into the box. The blanket made the box soft and full. He laid the duck on top. The box did not tip now. "There," said Elliot. "A bed for baby duck!"

Next, baby duck needed lunch. Elliot found a red play apple. "Juicy apple for you," he said. He held it to the duck's beak. Then he patted the duck's back, very gently. He sang a small song, "Sleep, baby, sleep."

Mom peeked in the door. "Is the baby sleeping?" she asked. "Shh," said Elliot. He covered the duck with a tiny sock. "Baby duck likes the sock," he whispered. "I like playing house, Mom. Come play too!"

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
story:
Isaiah went to the store with Mama. He held her hand on the busy street. At the door was a big bin of apples. Isaiah wanted a red one.

A girl was already at the bin. She picked apples one by one. Isaiah stood and waited. Mama said, "She goes first. Then it is your turn." So Isaiah kept waiting. The girl looked up. She said, "You can have a turn now." Isaiah picked a big red apple. The bin was full of apples, so there were plenty for both.

At the checkout, the line was long. Everyone stood one behind another. Isaiah stood behind a man with a full cart. Nobody pushed. Nobody ran. The line moved, step by step, all the way to the front. Isaiah put the apple on the belt all by himself.

Then the man with the full cart turned around. He held out a small sticker. "A star for waiting so nicely," he said. Isaiah pressed it onto his shirt. It was shiny gold. Isaiah smiled all the way home.

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
story:
Grayson got in the big car. "Campsite, campsite, campsite!" he yelled. Dad drove a long, long way. Mom said, "One tent, two bags, three snacks." Grayson counted too. "One, two, three!"

The tent went up. It was red and spotted. Grayson peeked inside. "My sleeping bag goes here!" But the wind began to blow. The tent's paper map flew off the table. It went up, up, up.

"My map!" Grayson yelled. He ran to Dad. Dad picked up a big rock. He put the rock on the corner of the map. The wind blew again. The map stayed still. The rock held it down.

Grayson found a small stone. He put his stone on the other corner. "I can help too!" The wind blew and blew. The map did not move at all. Grayson clapped his hands. Then he ran to get one more stone for Mom's hat, just in case.

activity: getting a first haircut at a salon
knowledge_domain: getting a first haircut at a salon
story:
Charlotte got her first haircut today. Her mama held her hand. They rode past the park on their bike. Then they came to the barbershop.

The barber was named Sam. Sam made the big chair go up. The chair could roll across the floor. "Whee," said Charlotte. Sam rolled the chair a little bit. Then he rolled it back.

Charlotte looked in the mirror. Her hair was long and curly. It stood up like a fluffy cloud. Sam filled a spray bottle with water. He sprayed her hair. The water made the curls fall down. The curls went flat and shiny. Now Sam could cut the straight wet hair.

"Is my hair weak now?" asked Charlotte. "No," said Sam. "It is just wet. Wet hair lies down flat. That helps the scissors." Charlotte watched. Snip, snip. The scissors cut a little piece. Snip, snip. Another piece fell. The pieces dropped onto the cape like dark rain.

Sam brushed the little pieces away. He took off the cape. Charlotte jumped down. Her hair was short and neat. She spun around in front of the mirror. "Mama, look at me!" said Charlotte. Mama clapped her hands.

activity: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
knowledge_domain: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
story: Luke woke up early. Today was the big family party! Grandma was coming, and Aunt May, and baby Sam too. Luke wanted to help make the bread. But the kitchen table was empty. "Where is the dough?" he asked. Mom laughed. "It is hiding," she said. "Come and see." She lifted a towel on a bowl. The dough had grown big and puffy! It had pushed the towel up like a little hill. "Wow!" said Luke. Mom said, "Now we can fold it." Luke patted the soft dough. It felt squishy like a pillow. He folded one side over. Then he folded the other side. "I did it!" said Luke. Grandma arrived with a big smile. "Something smells good!" she said. Luke jumped up and down. "I made bread! Come and see!" The oven was hot, so Dad put the bread in. Luke watched from his chair. Soon the bread was golden. Dad set it on the rack. Everyone sat down together. Luke tore a piece for Grandma. She took a big bite. "Mmm," said Grandma. "This is the best bread ever." Luke grinned. "More bread, please!"

activity: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
knowledge_domain: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
story:
Hailey stood by the big door of the grocery store. The cold air whooshed in every time it opened. She held her coat in her little hands.

"Can you do it all by yourself?" asked Mama.

"I can try," said Hailey.

She pushed one arm in. Then the other arm. The coat sat crooked on her shoulders. The zipper dangled far, far down. Hailey pulled the little slider up, but it would not move. She pulled again. Nothing happened.

"Why won't it go?" she asked.

"Look at the bottom," said Mama. "The two sides have to sit together first."

Hailey peeked down. The zipper ends were apart. She pushed them snug into one point. Then she pulled the slider. Ziiiip! All the way up to her chin.

"Cold air, go away!" said Hailey.

Mama laughed. They walked out to the car. There was a tiny pocket on the coat Hailey had never seen before. She unzipped part of the way, poked a finger in, and found a peppermint.

"Is this true? A candy pocket?" said Hailey.

"It sure is," said Mama. "But you have to zip up first. Cold hands can't hold candy."

Hailey zipped it up fast. She held the peppermint tight all the way home.

activity: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
knowledge_domain: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
story:
Jayden sat at the paint table at summer camp. His teacher Mia gave him three cups. "Red, yellow, blue," she said. Jayden pointed. "Red, yellow, blue," he said back. He tapped each cup as he named it. Red. Yellow. Blue.

Jayden wanted to paint a big green hill for his picture. But there was no green paint. He looked and looked. His lip wobbled. "No green," he said. "My hill is stuck." Mia sat down next to him. "Try mixing," she said. Jayden dipped his brush in the yellow. He dipped it in the blue. He swirled them together on his paper. The paint was cool and smooth under his brush. It made a big green blob!

Jayden clapped his hands. "I made green!" he said. He painted a big green hill with a red sun above it. His brush went swish, swish. "Look, Mia!" he said. Mia smiled. "That is a fine hill, Jayden."

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
story:
Henri sat on the train with Mama. They were going to Grandma's house for a family trip. Henri held his little blue bear. The train went clickety-clack, clickety-clack.

Henri wanted to see the cows in the fields. He looked out of the window. But the window was foggy and white. "Where are the cows?" he asked. "I can't see them." The window felt cold and wet when he touched it.

Mama took his hand. "Try this," she said. She helped him rub the window with his sleeve. Round and round his hand went. The fog wiped away in one little circle. "Now look," said Mama. Henri peeked through the circle. He saw a green field. He saw a big cow! The cow looked back at him.

The window fogged up again, so Henri rubbed a new circle. Each time it turned white, he wiped it clean, and the world came back. "I did it!" said Henri. He waved to the cow through the clear round hole. Then Mama gave him his warm cup of milk. The train went clickety-clack, and Henri watched the trees go by, round and round, wiping the window whenever it turned white.

activity: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
knowledge_domain: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
story:
Hudson stood at the little table in the art room. He had three pots of paint. One pot was red. One pot was yellow. One pot was blue.

"I want to paint a grape," said Hudson. "Grapes are purple." He looked and looked. There was no purple paint.

Miss Ana sat down next to him. "You can mix paints," she said. She put out a big clean tray. "Take your time."

Hudson dipped his brush in the blue pot. He made a blue spot on the tray. Then he dipped his brush in the red pot. He made a red spot on the blue spot. He stirred it round and round with the brush.

The paint turned purple. Hudson stopped stirring. He looked at it for a long time. Then he painted a big purple grape on his paper.

Next he wanted to paint a green leaf. He looked at his pots again. He put a yellow spot on the tray. He added some blue. He stirred slowly. The paint turned green.

Hudson hummed a little song while he painted. His brush went scratch, scratch on the paper. The purple grapes and the green leaves went home with him that day.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story:
Alice sat in her car seat. The sun was warm on her lap. "Are we there now?" she said.

"Not yet," said Mama. "We are driving now. We will see Grandma later."

Alice looked out the window. A red truck went by. Then a cow went by. The truck was loud. Then the cow was loud too. Alice laughed and opened her mouth wide to moo.

Yesterday, Alice had picked blueberries with Grandma. The basket had been heavy to carry. Today, the blueberries sat in a big jar at home. Tomorrow, Mama would make jam. Mama would cook it, and Alice would watch from her chair.

"First we drive," said Mama. "Then we eat lunch. Then we see Grandma."

Alice held up one finger. "First the cow!"

Mama laughed. "Yes. First the cow. Now here comes the bridge."

The car went up, up, up. Then it went down. Alice's tummy felt funny and good. "Again!" she said.

"Later," said Mama. "The bridge comes again later."

Alice watched the road. She waited for the bridge. Then she saw it, far away, small like a toy. "Bridge!" she said, and pointed her finger all the way there.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story:
Everly wanted the moon. She saw it in the sky last night. "Moon," she said. "Moon is up now too," said Mama. Everly looked out the window. The moon was big and white. But it was bedtime. "Can I hold the moon now?" asked Everly. "Not now," said Mama. "Later you can look again."

Mama tucked Everly into bed. "Yesterday you saw the moon too," said Mama. "You waved at it." Everly remembered waving. Her hand went up and down. The moon stayed in the sky. Everly waved again now. The moon did not come.

"I will get it tomorrow," said Everly. "Yes, tomorrow," said Mama. "First we sleep. Then it is a new day." Everly closed her eyes. She waited. She heard the wind outside. She heard Mama hum.

In the morning, Everly ran to the window. The sky was light. The moon was small and pale. "Moon stayed all night!" said Everly. She got a cup of water. She tasted it. She made a sour face. "This water tastes funny," she said. Mama laughed. "Here is fresh water." Everly drank it all. Then she waved at the pale moon. "Bye, moon. Come back tonight."

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story:
Ellie sat at the dinner table. Her bowl was empty. She wanted the special bread Grandma made.

"Yesterday we had Grandma's bread," said Ellie. "I want it now."

Mom smiled. "Grandma will bake a new loaf. But that is tomorrow. Today we have this bread."

Ellie looked at the bread in front of her. It was soft and white. She poked it with her finger. It did not look like Grandma's bread. Grandma's bread had seeds on top, like little brown boats.

Ellie pushed her plate away. "I don't want this bread."

Mom took a spoon of soup and poured it slowly. Drip, drip. Ellie watched the spoon. Then Mom tore the soft bread and dipped it in. The bread drank up the soup.

"You try," said Mom. "You can dip now."

Ellie picked up a small piece. She dipped it in her soup. It came out warm and wet. She took a bite. It was soft inside and good.

"Yum," said Ellie. She dipped another piece. Then another one.

Dad laughed. "Tomorrow, Grandma's bread. Today, dipping bread."

Ellie nodded. She kept dipping until her bowl was empty too.

"When is tomorrow?" she asked.

"After you sleep," said Mom. "First we sleep, then it is tomorrow."

Ellie yawned. She was not upset anymore. Her tummy was full.

"Can we have soup again tomorrow too?" she asked.

"We can have soup tomorrow too," said Dad.

Ellie rubbed her eyes and said, "Tomorrow, dipping bread and seeds."

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Dylan ran to the park with his red kite. The sun was warm on his face. The grass smelled fresh and green. He felt so excited.

Daddy held the kite up high. "Ready?" said Daddy. Dylan began to run. He pulled the string. But the kite did not go up. It sat on the grass. Dylan felt sad. His mouth turned down.

Then the wind came. Dylan saw the leaves start to dance. The wind pushed the kite right up into the sky. The red kite went higher and higher. Dylan laughed. He felt happy all over. He jumped up and down. "Look, Daddy! Look!"

A big dog ran by. It barked loud. Dylan held Daddy's hand. He felt scared for a minute. But the dog was only chasing a ball. It wagged its tail. Daddy said, "See, he is friendly." Dylan smiled again.

The wind stopped. The kite began to fall. Dylan stomped his foot. He felt angry. He wanted the kite to stay up. Then he remembered. He waited. He watched the leaves. They began to dance again. The wind pushed the kite back up. The sky was full of kites and birds. Dylan pulled the string with both hands.

"Again!" said Dylan. Daddy smiled. They ran together across the soft grass. The red kite flew above them.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story:
Yesterday, Anthony went to the library with Mama. He found a big red book about diggers. He took it home and read it three times.

Today, Anthony was hungry for more diggers. "Where is my red book?" he asked. He looked on the shelf. One blue book. One green book. One yellow book. No red book. "Maybe someone took it home," said the library lady. "It will come back later."

Anthony waited. He read a train book now. He stacked some soft blocks. Then he heard a bump. A red book slid down the return chute! It was the digger book. "It came back!" said Anthony. The library lady did smile. "You gave it back yesterday. Now it is here today." Anthony hugged the book tight. "Tomorrow I will bring it back again. And later, can we have cake?" Mama laughed. "Later, little one. Now let's check it out."

activity: going to the dentist for the first time
knowledge_domain: going to the dentist for the first time
story:
Sofia sat in the car with her teddy bear. "One bear, one Mama, one Sofia," she counted. They were going to the dentist for the first time. Sofia held teddy close. She was scared of the big chair.

The sun came through the window. It made a warm spot on her knee. Sofia moved her hand into the light. Her fingers turned bright and warm. She moved her hand away. The spot on her knee stayed warm.

"I can reach the sun spot," Sofia said. She reached out and patted teddy's ear. "The sun makes you warm, teddy." She put teddy in the light. Ted sat in the warm glow. Ted felt soft and cozy.

Mama parked the car. The dentist had a big wooden door. Sofia carried teddy inside. The chair was big, but she climbed up with help.

The dentist counted Sofia's teeth. "One, two, three," she said, all the way to twenty. Then Sofia held teddy up. "Count his teeth too," she said. The dentist smiled and gave teddy a little tap. Sofia grinned in the bright light.
